description: Proves bad input is refused (an attacker thumbprint given as ours, and Remove without a thumbprint or without a relay), that Detect and Remove on a runner with no ScreenConnect report CLEAN, read both registry views and write the UDF summary, and that a second run is harmless. Defender exclusions are skipped because GitHub's image excludes whole drives on purpose. Finding and removing planted indicators, and removing a real second client, are Tier 2 on an internal VM.

steps.label: Remove without known thumbprints is refused
Remove without a known relay is refused
A published attacker thumbprint given as ours is refused
Detect on a runner with no ScreenConnect is clean, and both registry views were read
UDF summary written where the Datto agent reads it
steps.name: Custom250

steps.label: Several thumbprints, upper case, separated by a semicolon and a space, are accepted
Remove with nothing to remove changes nothing
Remove with nothing found saves no evidence

Tier 2: on an internal VM with a planted C:\ProgramData\RelayTrap folder, a sckit-test file in C:\Windows\Temp, a harmless scheduled task named TrapWatch and a RelayTrapLiteAlert value under HKLM Run, Detect reports IOC_HIT
Tier 2: Remove on that VM deletes all four, saves evidence, and the re-check finds nothing left
Tier 2: on an internal VM with our client and a second ScreenConnect client from another instance, Remove (with our real thumbprint and relay) uninstalls the other one and ours keeps working
Tier 2: a real workstation shows its summary in the chosen Datto UDF after the agent's next check-in
